summary: McKean County, PA tower built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935, staffed in 1937 and 1939, removed before 1995; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Removed before 1995 per FFLOS; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

staffing.status: regular lookout named in April 1937 (Frank Kiess); a man sent to the tower in July 1939

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service, per FFLOS
Frank Kiess named regular lookout (Kane Republican item dated April 24, 1937)
Allegheny National Forest officials sent a man to the tower (Bradford Era item dated July 26, 1939)
Register says removed before 1995; the year is an upper bound, not a date
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: steel Aermotor tower built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1935.

evidence.supports: register lists no coordinates for the site
Frank Kiess named regular lookout on the Marshburg tower
evidence.quote: Frank Kiess has been named regular lookout on the Marshburg fire tower.

evidence.supports: Allegheny National Forest sent a man to the Marshburg tower
evidence.quote: The Allegheny National Forest officials have sent a man to the Marshburg tower already.

evidence.supports: no forest fires reported in the county in 1939
evidence.quote: No forest fires have been reported in this county

notes_for_editor: Brief lat/lon 41.8637, -78.7645 is not supported by the FFLOS page, which lists no coordinates; left unverified and not corrected. Only two short sources; the Forest Lookouts Pennsylvania entry has two dated items. Nothing found on the site today. The 1937 and 1939 items are newspaper transcriptions on Forest Lookouts, not the original papers.
